title: Information in Cognizable Cases (FIR Registration & Zero FIR)
chapter: Chapter XII: Information to the Police and Their Powers to Investigate
summary: Mandates procedure for recording First Information Report (FIR), introduces electronic communication of FIR (e-FIR) and Zero FIR.
fullText: Every information relating to the commission of a cognizable offence, if given orally to an officer in charge of a police station, shall be reduced to writing... Provided that information relating to the commission of any cognizable offence, irrespective of the area where the offence is committed, may be given (Zero FIR) and electronic communication may be taken on record.
plainExplanation: Enables citizens to file an FIR at any police station regardless of jurisdiction (Zero FIR) or register an e-FIR for cyber and bodily offenses, ensuring police cannot refuse registering serious complaints.
punishment: Procedural compliance mandated; refusal punishable under administrative and penal rules.
sourceDocument: Gazette of India, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Illustrative Mock Record)

title: When Police May Arrest Without Warrant & Notice of Appearance
summary: Specifies grounds under which police officers may arrest without warrant and guidelines on issuing notice of appearance for offenses punishable with less than 7 years.
fullText: Any police officer may without an order from a Magistrate and without a warrant, arrest any person who commits in his presence a cognizable offence... For offences punishable with imprisonment up to seven years, prior permission of Deputy Superintendent of Police is required for certain vulnerable categories and notice to appear shall precede arrest.
plainExplanation: Protects citizens from arbitrary arrest in minor or medium offenses by requiring police to issue an appearance notice first rather than immediate custodial arrest.
sourceDocument: Gazette of India, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Illustrative Mock Record)

title: Attachment, Forfeiture or Restoration of Property Derived from Crime
chapter: Chapter VIII: Reciprocal Arrangements & Seizure of Property
summary: Empowers courts and police to identify, attach, and freeze proceeds of cyber fraud, money laundering, or extortion.
fullText: Where the police officer conducting an investigation has reason to believe that any property is derived or obtained, directly or indirectly, as a result of a criminal activity, he may make an application to the Court for attachment or freezing of such property.
plainExplanation: Permits cyber crime cells and magistrates to quickly freeze scammer bank accounts and UPI wallets to restore stolen money to victims.
sourceDocument: Gazette of India, Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (Illustrative Mock Record)
